Q_H succeeds at level 1 (+0.634) because it reads that "which", and fails at levels 2-3 (+0.287/+0.393) because there the prefix is nearly an item identifier.

(2) Any functional of the SID prefix tree alone (Poincare tree embedding, LCA depth, tree distance between items) is a MONOTONE function of the depth of the lowest common ancestor, i.e. a graded same-bucket ratio - excluded by the contract and weak by the known result. So the curvature must act on the frozen reference geometry, not on the code tree. (3) With unit-norm reference vectors a fixed-radius exp-map puts every item on a sphere and the Poincare distance collapses to a monotone function of cosine -> "Euclidean in disguise". Therefore the design needs a NON-CONSTANT radial coordinate; I use the training-split target frequency (allowed input) as the radius profile, which is also the right allocation story (fine discrimination near the origin where query mass is, exponential room for rare items).

const ANS = `METRIC: HPSC
TITLE: Frequency-weighted Poincare silhouette margin of the level-1 code cells (hyperbolic level-1 decodability).
FORMULA: Let i = 1..N index items, N = 24587. Let c_i in {1..C} be the LEVEL-1 integer code of item i from the SID table, C = 256. Let u_i in R^d be the frozen reference representation of item i, L2-normalised so ||u_i||=1 (if the reference exposes separate source and target vectors, take u_i = normalise(normalise(src_i)+normalise(tgt_i)); otherwise use the source vector). Let f_i be the number of TRAINING-split pairs whose target is item i, and fmax = max_j f_j.
  H = ln C  (= ln 256 = 5.545177; the nats one code level can carry).
  alpha_i = H * ln(1+f_i) / ln(1+fmax);  r_i = tanh(alpha_i/2);  x_i = r_i * u_i in B^d (unit Poincare ball, curvature K = -1).
  Poincare distance: d(x,y) = arcosh( 1 + 2*||x-y||^2 / ((1-||x||^2)*(1-||y||^2)) ), with arcosh(1+z) = log1p(z + sqrt(z*(z+2))) and radii clamped to <= 1-1e-6.
  Weights w_i = 1 + f_i.
  For every non-empty cell S_c = { i : c_i = c }, compute the hyperbolic Frechet (Karcher) mean
     mu_c = argmin_{mu in B^d} sum_{i in S_c} w_i * d(mu, x_i)^2
  by 30 fixed iterations of mu <- exp_mu( sum_{i in S_c} w_i * log_mu(x_i) / sum_{i in S_c} w_i ), initialised at the member of S_c with the largest w_i (ties: smallest index), using the Mobius operations
     log_mu(x) = d(x,mu) * (mu (+) (-x)) / ||mu (+) (-x)||,  log_mu(mu) = 0,
     exp_mu(v) = mu (+) ( tanh(||v||/2) * v/||v|| ),  exp_mu(0) = mu,
     a (+) b = ((1+2<a,b>+||b||^2) a + (1-||a||^2) b) / (1+2<a,b>+||a||^2 ||b||^2).
  Per item: a_i = d(x_i, mu_{c_i})  (distance to its OWN cell centroid)
            b_i = min over non-empty cells c != c_i of d(x_i, mu_c)  (distance to the NEAREST WRONG cell centroid)
            s_i = (b_i - a_i) / max(a_i, b_i),  and s_i = 0 if max(a_i,b_i) = 0.
  HPSC = sum_i w_i * s_i / sum_i w_i, in [-1, +1], higher = better.
  Convention: if fewer than two cells are non-empty, HPSC := -1. No other branch, no randomness, no tuning.
INPUTS: (a) the exported Stage-2 SID table, level-1 integer code per item only; (b) the frozen Issue #126 behaviour reference, L2-normalised source/target vector per item (training-pairs-only by construction); (c) the TRAINING split, reduced to the target frequency f_i per item. Nothing else; no validation pair, no test pair, no recall value, no Stage-3 artefact.
GEOMETRY: Everything happens in the unit Poincare ball B^d with constant negative curvature K = -1. Curvature enters in three explicit places. (1) The item points ARE exponential-map images at the origin, x_i = exp_0(alpha_i * u_i) = tanh(alpha_i/2) u_i; alpha_i is a hyperbolic radius measured in nats of level-1 code capacity, ln C, scaled by log popularity. (2) Each cell centre is a true Frechet/Karcher barycentre on the manifold, computed with the hyperbolic log map at the current estimate - not a Euclidean average; in negative curvature the barycentre is pulled toward the dense core, and the pull is nonlinear in the radii, so it is not a rotated Euclidean centroid. (3) The margin s_i is a ratio of Poincare geodesic distances, and Poincare distance grows exponentially with radius, so an item parked in the sparse periphery is measured on an exponentially stretched ruler. The radial profile r_i is what keeps this honest: with unit-norm reference vectors and a single fixed radius the whole cloud would sit on a sphere, Poincare distance would degenerate to a monotone function of cosine, and the construction would be Euclidean in disguise; the log-popularity radius restores a genuine radial dimension, and it is also the correct capacity allocation (hyperbolic area is exponential, so dense query mass sits near the origin where the space is fine-grained and rare items get the room they need).
WHY IT SHOULD TRACK RECALL: Stage 3 decodes the level-1 token first, under a beam, from the query's behaviour representation; for the item to be recoverable at all the query must land nearer to the correct level-1 centroid than to any of the 255 wrong ones. s_i is exactly that condition, standardised per item, averaged under the training target-frequency measure - i.e. under (an estimate of) the very query/target distribution that test Recall@10 samples from. The scale behaves correctly at both ends: under a semantics-blind table every cell centroid collapses onto the global barycentre (near the origin), so a_i ~ b_i ~ r_i and HPSC -> 0; under a semantics-aware table the cell centroids move onto the cell's own behaviour region, a_i drops, b_i does not, and HPSC rises toward 1. It adds over Q_H in four ways: Q_H is a rank-agreement score on prefix scores and saturates once prefixes are near-tied, whereas HPSC is a first-moment geometric MARGIN that keeps resolving differences among good tables; Q_H is unweighted while HPSC is weighted by training target frequency (query mass); Q_H is a function of the ranking of prefixes only, while HPSC uses the frozen behaviour geometry the Stage-2 codebook was itself derived from, so it measures whether the code actually carved that geometry rather than whether prefix scores happened to order items well; and HPSC deliberately ignores levels 2 and 3, where Q_H is already known to collapse (+0.287 / +0.393) because the prefix is nearly an item identifier - a level-1-only construction avoids that dilution instead of averaging it in.
COMPUTE: 24587 items, d ~ 64, 256 non-empty cells of ~96 members. Karcher means: 256 * 30 * 96 ~ 7.4e5 log-map evaluations, each O(d) ~ 5e7 flops. Distances item-to-centroid: 24587 * 256 ~ 6.3e6 pairs, O(d) each ~ 4e8 flops plus 6.3e6 arcosh calls, done in row blocks of 2048 items (~50 MB peak). Fully vectorised float64 numpy, deterministic, no iteration over the 97 pairs and no training: 2-5 s single core, worst case well under a minute.
RISKS: The min over 255 centroids is an extreme statistic, so per-item noise in the frozen reference propagates; if the reference is weakly discriminative all b_i compress toward a_i and HPSC loses spread across the 97 tables even though its mean stays sensible. If the reference vectors are unit-norm and the training frequency profile is nearly flat (f_i roughly constant), r_i collapses to a constant, the cloud degenerates onto a sphere and HPSC becomes close to a monotone function of a cosine silhouette - still curved, but the curvature stops doing work; this is the main failure of the construction and it is detectable from the spread of alpha_i. a_i is mildly optimistic because item i contributes to mu_{c_i}, a bias of order 1/|S_c| ~ 1e-2 that is nearly identical across tables because cell sizes are near-uniform by construction. HPSC is undefined if the frozen reference or the training split is unavailable (I do not provide a fallback formula). Finally it is a level-1-only statistic, so it is blind to whether levels 2-3 are pathological, e.g. a table that is excellent at level 1 and fully collided below it.
FAILURE MODE: The table on which HPSC must be worst is the frequency-stratified random table: level-1 codes assigned by hashing item id (or by popularity quantile) rather than by behaviour. In the pure hash case every centroid sits at the global barycentre, a_i ~ b_i ~ r_i for all i, s_i ~ 0 and HPSC ~ 0 - indistinguishable from a merely mediocre table, i.e. it fails soft rather than soft-signalling. Worse, the popularity-quantile version actively fools it: it produces radially stratified cells (popular near the origin, rare at the boundary), which inflates b_i for rare items and yields a large HPSC with essentially zero Stage-3 recall. A second bad case is a table that keeps only a handful of level-1 codes alive (fewer than two non-empty cells hits the -1 convention, and a handful of giant cells pushes a_i toward r_i for everyone); and a third is a reference so weakly trained that all u_i are nearly parallel, which turns every d(x_i, mu_c) into a function of radii alone and makes HPSC a popularity statistic.
END METRIC`;
const r = await tools.progress.append_progress({content: "FINAL ANSWER (complete block, stands on its own):\n\n" + ANS});
console.log(JSON.stringify(r));

It adds over Q_H in four ways: Q_H is a rank-agreement score on prefix scores and saturates once prefixes are near-tied, whereas HPSC is a first-moment geometric MARGIN that keeps resolving differences among good tables; Q_H is unweighted while HPSC is weighted by training target frequency (query mass); Q_H is a function of the ranking of prefixes only, while HPSC uses the frozen behaviour geometry the Stage-2 codebook was itself derived from, so it measures whether the code actually carved that geometry rather than whether prefix scores happened to order items well; and HPSC deliberately ignores levels 2 and 3, where Q_H is already known to collapse (+0.287 / +0.393) because the prefix is nearly an item identifier - a level-1-only construction avoids that dilution instead of averaging it in.
COMPUTE: 24587 items, d ~ 64, 256 non-empty cells of ~96 members. Karcher means: 256 * 30 * 96 ~ 7.4e5 log-map evaluations, each O(d) ~ 5e7 flops. Distances item-to-centroid: 24587 * 256 ~ 6.3e6 pairs, O(d) each ~ 4e8 flops plus 6.3e6 arcosh calls, done in row blocks of 2048 items (~50 MB peak). Fully vectorised float64 numpy, deterministic, no iteration over the 97 pairs and no training: 2-5 s single core, worst case well under a minute.
RISKS: The min over 255 centroids is an extreme statistic, so per-item noise in the frozen reference propagates; if the reference is weakly discriminative all b_i compress toward a_i and HPSC loses spread across the 97 tables even though its mean stays sensible. If the reference vectors are unit-norm and the training frequency profile is nearly flat (f_i roughly constant), r_i collapses to a constant, the cloud degenerates onto a sphere and HPSC becomes close to a monotone function of a cosine silhouette - still curved, but the curvature stops doing work; this is the main failure of the construction and it is detectable from the spread of alpha_i. a_i is mildly optimistic because item i contributes to mu_{c_i}, a bias of order 1/|S_c| ~ 1e-2 that is nearly identical across tables because cell sizes are near-uniform by construction. HPSC is undefined if the frozen reference or the training split is unavailable (I do not provide a fallback formula). Finally it is a level-1-only statistic, so it is blind to whether levels 2-3 are pathological, e.g. a table that is excellent at level 1 and fully collided below it.
FAILURE MODE: The table on which HPSC must be worst is the frequency-stratified random table: level-1 codes assigned by hashing item id (or by popularity quantile) rather than by behaviour. In the pure hash case every centroid sits at the global barycentre, a_i ~ b_i ~ r_i for all i, s_i ~ 0 and HPSC ~ 0 - indistinguishable from a merely mediocre table, i.e. it fails soft rather than soft-signalling. Worse, the popularity-quantile version actively fools it: it produces radially stratified cells (popular near the origin, rare at the boundary), which inflates b_i for rare items and yields a large HPSC with essentially zero Stage-3 recall. A second bad case is a table that keeps only a handful of level-1 codes alive (fewer than two non-empty cells hits the -1 convention, and a handful of giant cells pushes a_i toward r_i for everyone); and a third is a reference so weakly trained that all u_i are nearly parallel, which turns every d(x_i, mu_c) into a function of radii alone and makes HPSC a popularity statistic.
